ecosystem.def: All the living things in an area together with the nonliving parts (water, soil, light, air) and the ways they interact.

population.def: All the individuals of one species living in the same area at the same time.

community.def: All the populations of different species that live and interact in the same area.

species.def: A group of similar organisms that can breed with one another and produce fertile offspring.

habitat.def: The place where an organism or population lives, with the conditions it needs.

biotic.def: Living, or once living: the organisms of an ecosystem and the dead matter they leave. Plants, animals, fungi and bacteria are biotic factors.

abiotic.def: Nonliving: the physical and chemical parts of an ecosystem, such as temperature, sunlight, water, minerals and wind.

predation.def: An interaction in which one organism (the predator) kills and eats another (the prey). The predator benefits and the prey is harmed.

competition.def: An interaction in which organisms use the same limited resource, so each gets less and both are harmed. It can be between species or within one species.

symbiosis.def: A close, long-term relationship between two different species: mutualism, commensalism or parasitism.

mutualism.def: A relationship between two species in which both benefit (+/+), such as bees and the flowers they pollinate.

commensalism.def: A relationship in which one species benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed (+/0).

parasitism.def: A relationship in which a parasite lives on or in a host and feeds on it, benefiting while the host is harmed (+/−), usually without being killed right away.

resource-partitioning.def: Species that compete for a resource dividing it by place, time or food size, which reduces competition so they can coexist.

niche.def: The role of a species in its ecosystem: what it eats, where and when it is active, and the conditions and resources it needs.
